title: The hard-subset labelling packet leaks its own selection criterion, contradicting the blinding claim in two graded documents
why_it_costs_marks: The one agreement figure that discriminates judge validity (0.750, n=8, versus the seed subset's non-discriminating 1.000) rests on a blinding claim the project invites the grader to verify by inspection — and the first artifact opened falsifies it. That is a materially inconsistent evaluation claim, which the rubric treats as a cap at 4.
evidence: docs/evidence/label-packet-hard-2026-09-22.md:3 prints 'subset `judge_lowest`'; line 5 then tells the labeller the criterion is 'recorded in the project's artifacts and **deliberately withheld from this packet**'. evaluation/REPORT.md:146 asserts 'It also disclosed neither the selection criterion nor the score ordering'; design-and-evaluation.md:1495 asserts 'the hard packet additionally withholds both the selection criterion and the score ordering'; :1501 says 'both packets are committed, so the blinding is inspectable rather than asserted'. The same sentence is frozen into evaluation/reference_labels_hard.yaml protocol.blinding and repeated at docs/evidence/README.md:63. scripts/gen_label_packet.py's HEADER interpolates 'subset `{subset}`' from the CLI value with no sanitisation, while its own module docstring names this exact hazard ('What must not happen is the labeller learning it'). The hard session is the only one of the two that returned a not_grounded, and it returned it on expenses-001, which the seed session labelled grounded.
fix: Render the header as `subset: (recorded elsewhere)` or a neutral token, regenerate both committed packets, and add a contract test asserting no packet contains a score, verdict, ordering hint or criterion-bearing subset name. If the packets cannot be re-labelled before submission, retract the 'disclosed neither the selection criterion' clause in evaluation/runner.py's report template and at design-and-evaluation.md:1495 and state plainly that the hard session could infer the criterion from the packet header.
effort: ~30 min to reword and retract; ~2 h plus a fresh blind session to regenerate and re-label

I re-derived from evaluation/results/r_1790110325_baseline.json (the run evaluation/results/latest.json names): items with tool_recall < 1.0 are remote-004 (0.75) and unsafe-001 (0.75), both passed=0. The same document tables both at :1374-1375 and narrates them at :1752-1761. The sentence was true of the 28-item round-1 run r_1790074972_baseline (tool_recall<1: []) and was not updated. title: The tools_disabled filter is enforced on the offered catalog but not at the MCP call boundary, so the published ablation arm calls a tool it disabled on 8 of 30 items
why_it_costs_marks: The rubric's ablation requirement is satisfied by an arm whose stated intervention did not fully happen, and the metric improvement the last wave is proudest of depends on the unfiltered call. It is an evaluation-validity defect with an MCP-layer cause, and the operator knob does not do what .env.example says.
evidence: src/hrmosaic/agent/router.py:211 unions MCP_TOOLS_DISABLED with the per-request list, but that union governs only the schema array offered to the model. `_settle_profile_debt` / `_profile_outstanding` (src/hrmosaic/agent/orchestrator.py:2058-2104) carries no `_permitted()` clause, unlike its siblings `_verdict_outstanding` (:2124) and `_propose_deterministically` (:2204), and `_call` (:2403) forwards straight to client.call_tool. I confirmed the consequence on the artifact: evaluation/results/r_1790111270_no_structured_tools.json lists lookup_employee_profile in config.tools_disabled, and 8 items record it in scores.tools_called (expenses-002, pto-002, pto-003, remote-003, remote-004, benefits-002, unsafe-001, unsafe-002). dataset.yaml gives remote-003 and remote-004 `requires_tool_results: [lookup_employee_profile]`, so their workflow 1.0 on that arm is produced by the disabled call. The two contract tests covering the knob read only `tools_offered` spans.
fix: Check `name in self._permitted(turn)` inside `_call` (or gate `_profile_outstanding` on `PROFILE_TOOL in self._permitted(turn)`), add a test that an operator-disabled lookup_employee_profile is absent from a turn that would otherwise settle the profile debt, then either re-drive the arm or annotate the published comparison with the 8 items that called it. Also record the effective union rather than the requested list at evaluation/runner.py:1050.
effort: ~1 h for the guard and test; a re-drive costs about $0.75 and one UTC day of cap headroom

title: check_policy_compliance attaches approvals and next steps derived from requirements it recorded as not_stated, and the deciding field is absent from the published schema
why_it_costs_marks: The tool asserts a conclusion it explicitly could not reach, contradicting its own published input contract, and the agent-layer mitigation repairs only the chat prose — an external MCP client on the documented public mount reads the unrepaired body. The disclosure is exemplary in mechanism but understates the blast radius and never mentions the instance that reaches `conditional` on the flagship demo scenario.
evidence: src/hrmosaic/mcpserver/rules.py:533 evaluates `unmet:<id>` as `not decided[id]`, decided[] holds decision.met (:783), and a not_stated row carries met=False by construction (:636) — while the published `unmet[]` list is correctly filtered on `status == "unmet"` (:832), so the body self-contradicts. Reproduced in-process: equipment_request with `{request_type: "refresh"}` returns verdict insufficient_evidence, `unmet: []`, and yet an early-refresh Direct-manager approval plus its next step; international_remote with only `destination_country` returns verdict **conditional**, `unmet: []`, and approvals [Direct manager, Director, Tax & Legal] with 'File a Tax & Legal review request at least 21 calendar days before departure' — byte-identical to the 42-day run. corpus/rules.yml has 18 `applies_when: "unmet:"` guards; the disclosure at design-and-evaluation.md:445-480 names only the four equipment ones. The deciding field `device_age_months` appears only at corpus/rules.yml:414 and nowhere in mcp/tools/check_policy_compliance.schema.json, whose `request_type` description defines "refresh" as a device at or past its 36-month cycle — the opposite of the approval reason returned.
fix: Split the guard vocabulary (`unmet:` meaning `status == "unmet"`, plus a separate `not_stated:` form), or suppress every `unmet:`-guarded approval and next step when the row is not_stated; name `device_age_months` in the parameters description. If the provenance freeze stands, widen the disclosure to state the real scope (18 guards, including international_remote's Tax & Legal approval at verdict `conditional`) and add characterisation tests pinning the current output for `{request_type: "refresh"}` and `{destination_country: "PT"}`.
effort: ~2 h plus a re-ingest-free re-drive for the code fix; ~30 min for the disclosure-and-freeze route

title: deployed.md's free-tier quota argument rests twice on a retention bound the live store contradicts by 2.9x
why_it_costs_marks: A false claim, stated twice, inside a section headed 'Nothing here is inferred', catchable by a grader who merely opens the URL the same document supplies. It also makes the read-cost arithmetic the paragraph prices unreliable, since per-poll rows scale with the number of eval runs committed.
evidence: deployed.md:580 and :595 both close with '`TRACE_RETENTION_SESSIONS = 300` bounds the store regardless'. src/hrmosaic/core/retention.py:29-35 (PRUNABLE_SESSIONS) exempts every session with a non-null eval_run_id, and its docstring says so. Live `/health` reports trace_store {backend turso, reachable true, session_count 856, span_count 20735, eval_runs_imported 29} against settings.py:140's default of 300. src/hrmosaic/web/api.py:2173-2177 issues three unqualified COUNT(*)s on every `/health` call with no cache, plus count_calls_today and _last_llm_call — the five queries the paragraph prices — and the 379k-rows-read figure it relies on was read 2026-09-10 against a near-empty store and has never been re-derived.

Then either re-read Turso usage on the current store or cheapen `/health` (cache the three counts for ~30 s, or use max(rowid)) so the quota claim is derived from today's shape.
effort: ~20 min to reword; ~1 h if the /health counts are also cached

title: The chunking strategy is described as sentence-boundary overlap in shipped source and two graded documents; 23 of 29 continuation windows begin mid-word
why_it_costs_marks: A false statement about the design choice R2.2 grades, repeated in three places, and untested — a grader who greps the manifest after reading the justification finds the opposite. The damaged text is also what the reader would see in a citation blockquote and what the model sees in the `<document>` envelope.
evidence: src/hrmosaic/rag/chunk.py:146 snaps the window end to a boundary via `_cut`, but :155 starts the next window at `max(end - overlap_chars, start + 1)` — a raw offset. chunk.py:6-7 claims windows are 'cut on sentence boundaries so a chunk never begins mid-sentence'; design-and-evaluation.md:238 and :2021 say '150 characters of overlap on sentence boundaries'; .env.example:56 repeats it. Over data/index/chunks.manifest.jsonl there are 29 continuation windows; 23 begin mid-word (e.g. c_598a56bc1ec155da opens 'n there is not available.'), the other 6 mid-sentence. The stored snippet column carries the damage. tests/unit/test_chunking.py has no assertion on a continuation opening. Mitigating: CHANGELOG.md:662-668 already discloses the phenomenon accurately, so this is an internal inconsistency, and neither committed demo cites one of the 29.
fix: Cheapest: correct the three claims to say the end cut is on a sentence boundary and the overlap start is not, and state the 29-window figure. Better: snap the continuation start backwards to the nearest sentence (or at minimum word) boundary before slicing — which moves every chunk_id and needs a re-ingest, manifest rewrite and re-drive.
effort: ~20 min for the wording; ~3 h plus a re-drive for the code fix

title: 'The run pinned on this build' is false — the task-1 capture measures a superseded application build

The capture ran against /health sha 8782177 over app build 8a89310; `git diff --stat 8a89310..HEAD -- src mcp Dockerfile render.yaml requirements.txt` is 14 files / +275 / -54, including check_policy_compliance.py and search_policy_documents.py. The phrase landed at 70b095c, after 80a5a71. title: The action-safety denominator is keyed to expectation rather than violation, so a real unsafe write outside the two unsafe_action items would not lower the published rate
why_it_costs_marks: The metric whose job is to catch an unconfirmed write is the one metric that would exclude the item on which it happened, and its population choice is published in the design doc but not on the report line.
evidence: evaluation/runner.py:832-836 builds the population from safety_at_stake, which runner.py:561-563 sets to `bool(usage.gated) or item.category == 'unsafe_action' or item.expected_behavior == 'confirm'`. The per-item score is computed for all 30 items (runner.py:518), but a turn that performs an unconfirmed write has no gated span (the gate is what produces CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED, deterministic.py:361-376), so such an item would score 0.0 and be excluded. On the published run only unsafe-001 and unsafe-002 carry safety_at_stake, n=2 of 30. Mitigating, and why this is low rather than higher: the 0.0 still reaches the composite for every item (runner.py:576-582, deterministic.py:693 'action-safety 0.00 < 1.00'), so it would drop strict_pass_rate over n=30 and be named in REPORT.md's failure table; and orchestrator.py:3474-3478 makes a gated span a precondition of the only tokened write path, so the excluded case needs a separate gate bug.
fix: Add `or safety == 0.0` to the safety_at_stake predicate — any observed violation is by definition at stake — and state the population on evaluation/REPORT.md's action-safety line the way design-and-evaluation.md:1216-1222 already does.

title: The orchestrator makes non-RAG tool calls on a policy_qa turn, and only the code says so
why_it_costs_marks: A grader comparing the routing section with dashboard page 3 for remote-003 sees an apparent contradiction with nothing in the documentation to resolve it, and the lifecycle diagram never shows that the orchestrator itself can call tools and propose writes the model never chose.

The call below is the orchestrator's, not the model's', and :2090-2113 issues the call. Live turn 1553f812c9a019955fb8e8fb104caa05: intent policy_qa, every act llm_call offering only the four RAG tools, then span 21 tool_call lookup_employee_profile with catalog_reopened false. design-and-evaluation.md:533-538 presents the gate as 'the people-data and write tools are not in the array at all' and its lifecycle diagram at :120-141 omits the profile debt, the data debt, the action debt and the deterministic verdict scoring. Mitigating: :1884-1889 does disclose the profile-debt repair by name, the trace self-describes via a `profile_read_deterministically` nudge, and the action debt and verdict scoring do consult `_permitted`.

title: The dashboard's own smoke-eval button can silently replace an ablation arm on the compare tab
why_it_costs_marks: One admin click can put a 3-item run under the heading 'Ablation — three variants over the identical items', charted against two 30-item arms with flips recomputed against it, and the existing build-mismatch alert cannot fire for a run with no committed file.
evidence: src/hrmosaic/web/dashboard.py:3087-3090 pairs `newest.setdefault(row['variant'], row)` over `SELECT ... ORDER BY created_at DESC` with no filter on n_items, target or label, although RUN_COLUMNS (:2789) already selects n_items. SmokeEvalBody (:3152-3155) defaults variant to baseline and n_items to 3, and evals.html:101-108 preselects both. Smoke rows do reach the store (evaluation/runner.py:350, :1087, :1870-1871). `_target_git_sha` (:3030-3047) returns None with no committed file and :3104 drops None from the build set, so builds_differ stays False. Heading at evals.html:126. Mitigating: evals.html:205-210 warns in-page that the charted arms are the newest per variant and 'are not always' the published comparison's runs, the arms table prints each run id and a muted em dash for the missing build, and the flip loop skips items absent from baseline. Live compare tab is clean: all three arms on 80a5a71, builds_differ false, 10 flips.

title: Task 2's 1:20 chat-page budget silently omits a second full agent turn
why_it_costs_marks: About 115-120 s of content is scheduled into an 80 s frame, and unlike task 1 the row states no wait allowance, so the presenter has no cue that 'ask again' is a second turn. Total headroom is 45 s against the 10:00 ceiling.
evidence: docs/demo-script.md:81 allots 'Chat page and the confirmation card (≈ 1:20)'; :297-324 asks inside it for send, card, a 40-second safety beat ('do not rush this'), 'Don't open it' plus the cancelled receipt, 'Ask again, reaching the card a second time', then 'Open the request' plus the lede. From docs/evidence/demo-task-2-live-2026-09-22.txt: spans 1-20 (send to card) sum to 20.8 s and spans 23-36 (confirm resume) to 12.6 s; the decline press is not free either, since orchestrator.py:1168-1183 re-runs `_answer`. So about 65 s of waiting plus the 40 s beat plus two receipts. Task 1's row states an allowance ('Budget the turn itself at ~40 s ... allow up to 50 s'); task 2's states none.
fix: Give the task-2 row an explicit wait budget ('two turns of about 35 s each plus two confirm resumes — roughly 65 s of waiting; the safety beat is spoken while the first card is up, so budget the chat frame at 2:00') and re-chain the table, or make the cancel path a stated optional cut.

title: The published coverage denominator is stale (10,298 statements against the shipped 10,320) and its guard degrades to a document-agreement check
why_it_costs_marks: A published figure a grader can re-derive differs from the artifact, and the existing guard passes only because the local coverage.xml predates three src-touching commits — so a clean clone that runs `make coverage` twice gets a red contract test.
evidence: README.md:70-71 and design-and-evaluation.md:1022 publish '95% of statements and 88% of branches over 10,298 statements' as measured 2026-09-22. coverage.xml is untracked, timestamped 13:09Z, before the round-2 commits at 80a5a71; the tip CI run prints 'TOTAL 10320 472 2518 259 94%', and parsing the HEAD tree with coverage's own PythonParser gives 10,320 / 2,518 (10,298 / 2,512 for the pre-80a5a71 tree). tests/contract/test_docs_completeness.py:943-1044 already implements the parse-and-compare guard, but returns None when coverage.xml is absent — which is the CI test job's state and, locally, the state before `coverage xml` runs — so it falls back to asserting the documents agree with each other. Percentages are unaffected.
fix: Re-read the figure off the tip run (10,320) or regenerate coverage.xml at HEAD and repaste both sites. To close the guard properly, run `coverage xml` before a second targeted `pytest tests/contract/test_docs_completeness.py -k coverage` in the CI test job, or have the gate step fail on a documented-versus-measured mismatch directly.
effort: ~10 min for the figure; ~30 min for the CI ordering

title: docs/architecture.html's footer dates the page 2026-09-09 and names the superseded frozen spec as its source
why_it_costs_marks: The page's only provenance line points a grader at the document whose own banner says it is superseded on exactly the points the page now publishes correctly, so the reader either distrusts a current page or trusts the wrong source of truth. No test guards any numeric figure on it, which is why it had to be hand-repaired in both fix waves.
evidence: docs/architecture.html:1491-1496 'Design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-hr-agentic-rag-design.md · generated 2026-09-09'. That line has never been edited (`git log -p` shows one hunk, in creation commit f8bd62d), while the page has 20 commits touching it, the last three on 2026-09-22 (a0b37a6, 68d9cdb, 399d807). The spec's banner at :3-25 lists the span rail, four-versus-five jobs, ~280 versus 205 chunks and the 28-item planning set as superseded — all figures the page now states correctly (205 chunks, 30 items, five jobs, deploy needing ux). `grep -c design-and-evaluation docs/architecture.html` returns 1, inside an HTML comment, so nothing rendered points at the current design of record.
fix: Change the footer to 'Current design of record: design-and-evaluation.md · page last revised 2026-09-22 (build 80a5a71)'. If the class is worth guarding, add three assertions to tests/contract/test_docs_completeness.py that the page's chunk count, dataset size and job count match the manifest, dataset.yaml and ci.yml.
effort: ~5 min for the footer; ~45 min with the assertions

title: docs/process/sdd/G5-grade-5/README.md indexes round 1 only, while ai-tooling.md sells that README as where the disclosure is checked
why_it_costs_marks: A self-cited disclosure artifact whose stated inventory is provably wrong — the same unsupported-map class both earlier grades opened with. Its 'Every file here was scanned before it was copied' assurance now silently extends over 28 round-2 files with no recorded scan.
evidence: docs/process/sdd/G5-grade-5/README.md:12 'the fixes themselves are the `G5(…)` commits from `98c893f` onward' (round 2 landed as `G5b(…)` from 9dcd8dd) and :26 '**Coverage: 9 briefs and 13 reports** over tasks 1, 1b, 1c, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5b and 6a-6e'. Actual: 12 briefs, 28 reports, plus regrade-report.md and regrade-gaps.json with no inventory row. `grep -n 'G5b\|round 2\|regrade\|re-grade' README.md` returns nothing. ai-tooling.md:366-367 points at it 'with a `README.md` there naming what was left out of the copy and how every file was scanned for credentials first'. `git log -5 -- .../README.md` shows only the round-1 commit a040074, while HEAD 39dc61c copied the 28 files across. title: The retired 0.26 retrieval threshold still lives in both committed golden trace fixtures
why_it_costs_marks: Last residue of the round-2 schema sweep, and it is exactly the number a grader greps for after reading the retirement paragraph. The dashboard pretty-prints the whole span payload, so a fixture-driven render displays a threshold the shipped system never uses.
evidence: tests/fixtures/traces/remote_work_eligibility.json:279 and tests/fixtures/traces/pto_request_confirmed_write.json:287 both carry `"min_dense_score": 0.26`. The shipped floor is 0.45 (settings.py:110, .env.example:51) and the schema now publishes `"default": null` naming MIN_SUPPORT_SCORE. The only emitter, src/hrmosaic/mcpserver/tools/search_policy_documents.py:205-220, writes the resolved threshold, and the project's own real capture (docs/evidence/demo-task-1-live-2026-09-15-session.json) records 0.45 on all six retrieval spans — so the fixtures never matched observed behaviour. Conceded internally at docs/process/sdd/G5-grade-5/task-10-report.md:257-260 ('now misleading ... Left alone deliberately') but absent from the graded limitations list.

title: The design doc's error-semantics row overstates the retry, which mcp/README.md already words correctly in two rows
why_it_costs_marks: The document a grader reads for graceful error handling says a transport failure is retried once, which is false for a tools/call — the no-retry path that is the fail-safe direction for a possibly-executed write.
evidence: design-and-evaluation.md:495 '**Transport failure** → the client re-discovers once, then emits an `error` span'. src/hrmosaic/agent/client.py:567-569 raises McpUnavailable on a tools/call transport error with no retry and no reset, and every orchestrator catch routes to `_degraded` (orchestrator.py:3127-3162), which never re-discovers. The only retry is `_discover`, whose docstring at :1637 says so: 'a `tools/call` that fails degrades the turn immediately'. mcp/README.md:150-151 already splits the two rows correctly.
fix: Split the design-doc row the way mcp/README.md does: transport failure at discovery gets one re-discovery; transport failure on a tools/call degrades immediately and is never re-sent.

title: deployed.md mis-describes what est_cost_usd covers, so the all-in measurement bill excludes about 25 judge passes
why_it_costs_marks: A wrong gloss on the one cost figure the document publishes as its honest overrun, and the table is self-contradictory: the row above prices the judge separately while this row claims it is already inside the total.
evidence: deployed.md:488 '$16.25 across the 25 committed evaluation runs — the sum of their `est_cost_usd` (agent plus judge spans, each priced at write time)'. The sum is right ($16.2534 over 25 files, range $0.4159-$0.8926), but est_cost_usd is `sum(entry.cost_usd for entry in scored)` over scored target turns (runner.py:1020, :612; deterministic.py:547-549), and judge calls are written to a separate `eval_judge` session (runner.py:377-388, 629-631). Confirmed in the store: for r_1789032950_baseline the `eval` session's 91 llm_calls sum to 0.435482 — exactly the run file's est_cost_usd — while its `eval_judge` session's 293 calls contribute nothing. Nine of 25 runs were judged at roughly $0.16-0.18 a pass, so the honest all-in figure is about $1.4-1.6 higher; warmup turns (~$0.36 total) are also excluded. The same misconception is in a comment at evaluation/runner.py:1225.
fix: Say 'the sum of their est_cost_usd (the scored agent turns; judge spans are written to a separate `eval_judge` session and warmup turns are excluded)' and add the judged-run judge estimate as its own addend. Fix the runner.py:1225 comment too.

title: A committed cold-start artifact and two graded documents still name da0dca2 as the build that served the published run
why_it_costs_marks: A false provenance label on the source of the 71.0 s median the deployment segment narrates, and deployed.md contradicts itself — its own run ledger marks that build's run 'no — prose only' 180 lines above the sentence saying it served the published run.
evidence: docs/evidence/cold-start-probes.json:24 and :36 set build to 'the final build (Waves 1-2), the one that served the published evaluation run' for probes on da0dca2 (2026-09-11). The published run is r_1790110325_baseline on 80a5a71. The same clause appears at deployed.md:244 and docs/optimization-log.md:309, against deployed.md:63's own row for r_1789086979_baseline ('da0dca2 | no — prose only'). docs/evidence/README.md:5-12 and :27 set a global policy that older 'final build' headers mean final as of that date, but quote only that half and never correct the 'served the published evaluation run' clause — and that policy covers evidence headers, not maintained prose. Mitigating: the probe segments are checkable against a committed ledger (docs/process/sdd/progress.md:366), so the transcription is verifiable.

title: The judge-pass token totals behind the cost estimate have no committed artifact, and the sentence stating them is self-undermining
why_it_costs_marks: An unverifiable figure inside an otherwise scrupulous report, whose stated premise is false — judge tokens are recorded — and which appears to attribute one pass's measured tokens to a different pass's call count.
evidence: evaluation/REPORT.md:117-121 says 'Nothing records judge *tokens*, so the totals below are the ones measured on run `r_1789055103_baseline` — ~369k input and ~20k output over 264 calls'. That run file has no token fields, the trace store is git-ignored, and grep for the totals finds only prose. But judge calls do carry tokens (evaluation/judges.py:13-16; core/llm/openai_compat.py:233-234; core/trace.py:683-684): summing the local store's eval_judge llm_calls gives 369,325 in / 19,987 out over 232 calls for r_1789032950_baseline (whose judge_calls is 232), reproducing the $0.16 to the cent — while REPORT.md attributes those tokens to r_1789055103_baseline 'over 264 calls', a run with no eval_judge session in the store.
fix: Derive the figure from the store with one SUM over eval_judge llm_call spans and name the run it actually came from, or state the external source explicitly ('read off the Gemini console for that pass on 2026-09-10; not reconstructible from the repository'). Correct the 'nothing records judge tokens' premise at runner.py:1228-1229.

title: README's before/after row pairs two hard-subset agreement figures that are not comparable
why_it_costs_marks: The row invites a regression reading of 1.000 to 0.750 when the two figures are over different item sets labelled by different blind sessions against different runs, and nothing on or beside the row says so.
evidence: README.md:316 '| Judge agreement (hard subset, selection disclosed) | 1.000 (n = 8) | 0.750 (n = 8) |', inside a table framed at :301-303 as the pre-optimization set beside the published run — with a caveat about item count that does not describe a score-selected 8-item subset. The subset is recomputed per run (evaluation/schema.py:441-467): the earlier label file (git show d0cc8ee) covers leave-001 and pto-003 where HEAD's covers equipment-001 and remote-004. The earlier 1.000 was itself eight unanimous grounded labels — the same non-discriminating matrix the docs criticise for the seed subset. The same unflagged pairing appears in design-and-evaluation.md's seven-column table. Mitigating: the earlier figure is reproducible from history (I re-derived 1.000, n=8), and the per-run re-authoring policy is stated in the design doc.
fix: Footnote the row: the two subsets are different item sets labelled by different sessions against different runs, and the earlier figure is history rather than a baseline for this one.

title: Two independent renderers of the same headline table disagree about which metrics have design targets
why_it_costs_marks: One run appears in two published tables whose Target columns say different things, and every threshold is a duplicated string literal, so a threshold change needs edits in two files with nothing reconciling them.
evidence: evaluation/runner.py:1524 sets a Target only for strict pass, so evaluation/REPORT.md:26/28/34 render '–' for groundedness, cit_resolve and action safety. scripts/paste_eval_numbers.py:47-61 hard-codes '≥ 0.90', '≥ 0.95', '1.00', 'lower is better' and '≥ 0.85' into design-and-evaluation.md:1157-1174, and imports nothing from runner — so even the strict-pass target is an independent literal. tests/contract/test_docs_completeness.py:643-655 binds row labels only; tests/unit/test_report_states_the_target.py:48-49 pins the em dashes. Both target sets are individually defensible (the extra ones trace to the spec and docs/requirements-traceability.md:222); they are simply not reconciled.

title: The rules engine reads 'could not check' as 'checked and failed', and the disclosure understates the class by 14 guards
why_it_costs_marks: Same root cause as rank 4, viewed from the guardrail side: the disclosure is unusually candid but names only the equipment instances and never mentions that the same class attaches Director and Tax & Legal approvals on international_remote at verdict `conditional` rather than `insufficient_evidence`, and nothing pins the deferred behaviour.
evidence: corpus/rules.yml carries 18 `applies_when: "unmet:"` guards; design-and-evaluation.md:445-480 and limitation 13 at :1844-1864 cite four (all equipment). `grep -rn 'guard_holds' tests/` returns one line, testing only the unknown-prefix error, so the disclosed-and-deferred behaviour is unfrozen. The remote path is reachable outside the workflow's slot protection because check_policy_compliance is in the hard-restricted policy_qa catalog and remote-003 is policy_qa-routed on the published run. Mitigating: src/hrmosaic/agent/compliance.py:388-444 appends an explicit 'I could not check the <topic> requirement' line for every not_stated row, remote.intl.annual_limit is blocking-and-not_stated so writes still refuse, and the published run's two international_remote items both supplied dates (groundedness 1.000 and 0.969), so the disclosure's bound holds.
fix: Widen the disclosure to state the real scope (18 guards, of which the international_remote Tax & Legal approval reaches a `conditional` verdict), and add characterisation tests pinning the current output for `{request_type: 'refresh'}` and `{destination_country: 'PT'}` so the deferred behaviour cannot drift unrecorded.

title: The expense workflow's served answer justifies the approver from the wrong rule
why_it_costs_marks: The workflow that exists because a USD 3,000 question was once answered from the USD 2,500 row now leads with the wrong threshold again, the compliance restatement step did not fire, and the design doc frames the resulting failure mainly as a judge-versus-labeller disagreement.
evidence: Live turn 67dc4d8653ec7a7f0b0c92bda4dc67d2 span 18 records expense.manager_limit met false / status unmet ('parameters.amount_usd is 3000; the policy value is 2500'), approvals including Director, and the next step 'Ask a director to approve'. The served prose leads 'Since your USD 3,000 conference trip is below the USD 5,000 director threshold, your manager Dana can approve it', then partly contradicts itself. The judge scored that claim contradicted (groundedness 0.778, one of the run's three composite failures). I reproduced why the repair misses: compliance.py's polarity() returns 'denies' for that sentence and relation() maps denies-against-unmet to 'agrees', so correct() leaves it, and correct_ceilings only matches 'up to USD X'. design-and-evaluation.md:1391-1399 and :1795 read the loss as the judge being the stricter reader. Mitigating: Dana is in fact the resolved Director for both tiers, and the correct routing rule is stated and cited in the next sentence.
fix: Extend the restatement: when a requirement row is unmet on a threshold, refuse any sentence concluding the lower authority may approve and substitute the engine's own routing sentence, then re-drive. If deferred, add one line to the limitation naming the defect (the lead sentence cites the wrong threshold) rather than only the judge disagreement.
effort: ~1 h plus a re-drive; ~10 min for the disclosure line

title: '69 screen ids' is a stale capture count given three different values in three documents
why_it_costs_marks: A number a grader can falsify by running the command the README invites them to run — `make ux-capture` prints 72, and one document explicitly claims 69 is the number that run prints.
evidence: README.md:149 'make ux-capture re-photographs all 69 screen ids'; docs/evidence/ux-final/README.md:8 and :18-19 repeat 69, the latter as 'the number make ux-capture prints at the end of its own run'; docs/evidence/README.md:88 hedges to '69 to 71'. .ux-capture/index.json (generated 2026-09-15T23:33, after the last change to scripts/ux_capture.py) records 72 unique ids over 390 entries, and scripts/ux_capture.py:1020 prints that count. The repo's own newest audit, docs/evidence/ux-reaudit-4-2026-09-16.md:17, says 72. The geometry property itself holds (0 of 390 entries report body_horizontal_scroll).

effort: ~15 min for the wording; ~45 min with the assertion

title: README says `make setup` runs exactly the printed steps, and the dev-dependency list omits coverage and the ux group
why_it_costs_marks: Trivially falsifiable by a grader reading the Makefile beside the README in a repository whose stated discipline is that a printed command is executable as printed. The sharper half is that `make ux` cannot work from a README-only setup, with no documented remedy.
evidence: README.md:37 '`make setup` runs exactly those steps' against Makefile:22-26, which adds `pip install --upgrade pip` and omits the (explicitly optional) `cp .env.example .env`. README.md:367 describes the development-only set as 'pytest, ruff and fpdf2, pinned in requirements-dev.txt' while coverage==7.10.7 is in that manifest and is what the CI gate runs. `grep -rn 'requirements-ux\|playwright' README.md` returns nothing, yet Makefile:77-78 runs `make ux` against the setup venv, which never installs that group — only CI does (.github/workflows/ci.yml:139, 149-150).
fix: Soften the sentence ('`make setup` runs those steps and upgrades pip first; `.env` is left to you'), add coverage and the ux group to Third-party components, and document `pip install -r requirements-ux.txt && python -m playwright install chromium` beside `make ux`.

title: `make test` has an undocumented hard dependency on `make ingest`
why_it_costs_marks: A fresh clone that runs the common reflex `make setup && make test` gets a red suite, and the failure is a bare sqlite error with no remediation hint.
evidence: 15 test files read the built index through core.corpusread, and CI orders `ingest --verify-manifest` before the suite with the comment 'it leaves a real index for the suite' (.github/workflows/ci.yml:98). README ties ingest only to `make run` (:42, :55) and describes `make test` as self-contained (:63-77); the dependency is stated only in internal process docs. Reproduced: `INDEX_PATH=/tmp/none.sqlite pytest -q tests/unit/test_g2_citation_resolvability.py` gives 15 failed / 2 passed at src/hrmosaic/core/corpusread.py:114 with OperationalError 'unable to open database file' — not the friendly FileNotFoundError at index.py:233, because corpusread.connect() does no existence check.
fix: Change the README comment to 'build the index first — `make run` and `make test` both need it', or give the `test` target an order-only prerequisite on data/index/hr_index.sqlite. Adding an existence check to corpusread.connect() would also surface the documented remedy.

title: `paths-ignore` still excludes `docs/**`, contradicting the rationale written directly above it
why_it_costs_marks: The comment argues that docs contract tests must gate the commits most likely to introduce a stale claim, then ignores the tree those tests read — and three commits in this wave touch only ignored paths, so pushed alone any could have falsified a contract test with no run. Three graded documents also describe `docs/**` as a published-results path, which it is not.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:13 `paths-ignore: ['evaluation/results/**', 'evaluation/REPORT.md', 'docs/**']` against the comment at :10-12. tests/contract/test_published_run_commands.py:227-231 reads docs/requirements-traceability.md and docs/pre-submission-checklist.md; test_docs_completeness.py binds docs/demo-script.md. a0b37a6, 70b095c and 39dc61c each touch zero non-ignored files and ran only because they rode along in a batch push. deployed.md:89-90, design-and-evaluation.md:1008-1009 and docs/demo-script.md:84 all call the three ignored paths the places 'a published *result* lands'. Mitigating: `pull_request:` carries no path filter, so PRs are fully gated, and the graded tip is green.
fix: Drop `docs/**` from paths-ignore (leaving the two published-result paths), or narrow it to subtrees no test reads (docs/process/sdd/**, docs/evidence/ux-*/**) and correct the three documents' description of what is skipped.

title: Small residual stale or incomplete figures in documents the demo shows or narrates
why_it_costs_marks: Each is trivial, but each sits on a surface the recording shows, and the paths-ignore panel is the one a grader could read as a complete list.
evidence: (a) docs/architecture.html:1343-1344 prints 'paths-ignore: docs/**, evaluation/results/**' — two of three, with no ellipsis, while the page uses one elsewhere; its detail card D["f6-t1"]:1803 is correct. (b) deployed.md:534's memory-gate log — the source of the 294.9 MB the deployment segment reads out — records chunk_count=204 from build 415f358; reconciled at deployed.md:86 and :132, so this is defensible as a dated capture.
